gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on August 23?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 23 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Munich Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/de/munich/EDDM.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from multiple models, including GFS runs, indicate Munich's August 23 high will hover near the 1991–2020 climatological average of 23.5°C under mostly clear to partly cloudy skies with light northerly winds and negligible precipitation. This tight clustering around 22–23°C explains the near-even market-implied odds, as small differences in daytime insolation, boundary-layer mixing, or minor advection from surrounding high pressure can shift the peak by 1°C. Historical analogs show late-August maxima routinely vary ±2°C day-to-day, while official DWD and ECMWF guidance released in the past 24 hours has shown minimal run-to-run spread, leaving traders with limited new data to differentiate the two leading outcomes before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Traders price Tokyo’s August 23 maximum near 30–31 °C because Japan Meteorological Agency and ensemble forecasts indicate a cloudy day with scattered showers or thundery activity that will limit afternoon heating. Typical late-August climatology shows a 30.5 °C normal high, yet persistent cloud cover and precipitation reduce insolation enough to cap peaks at or below 31 °C on most model runs. Differentiating the tightly bunched 30 °C (40 %) and 31 °C (35 %) outcomes hinges on the exact timing and coverage of showers: earlier or heavier rain suppresses the peak toward 30 °C, while delayed or lighter activity allows brief clearing that pushes the official reading to 31 °C. Lower-probability 32 °C scenarios require stronger subsidence and reduced moisture than currently modeled, while sub-29 °C outcomes remain unlikely absent an unforecasted cold front. Updated JMA guidance and real-time observations through the afternoon will resolve the remaining uncertainty before market settlement.

eventMetadata.context_description: Traders price Tokyo’s August 23 maximum near 30–31 °C because Japan Meteorological Agency and ensemble forecasts indicate a cloudy day with scattered showers or thundery activity that will limit afternoon heating. Typical late-August climatology shows a 30.5 °C normal high, yet persistent cloud cover and precipitation reduce insolation enough to cap peaks at or below 31 °C on most model runs. Differentiating the tightly bunched 30 °C (40 %) and 31 °C (35 %) outcomes hinges on the exact timing and coverage of showers: earlier or heavier rain suppresses the peak toward 30 °C, while delayed or lighter activity allows brief clearing that pushes the official reading to 31 °C. Lower-probability 32 °C scenarios require stronger subsidence and reduced moisture than currently modeled, while sub-29 °C outcomes remain unlikely absent an unforecasted cold front. Updated JMA guidance and real-time observations through the afternoon will resolve the remaining uncertainty before market settlement.

eventMetadata.context_description: Official forecasts from the Japan Meteorological Agency and supporting numerical models indicate a Tokyo daytime maximum near 31°C on August 23 under mostly cloudy skies, scattered showers, and light northeasterly winds near the seasonal climatological average of 30.7°C. Recent observations show midday temperatures approaching 30°C with high humidity around 70% and dew points near 24°C, while persistent cloud cover and precipitation chances of 20–30% limit intense solar heating and convective buildup that could push readings higher. Ensemble guidance shows limited spread around this outcome, consistent with recent days’ pattern of 31–33°C highs, though brief afternoon clearing could allow a one-degree upward nudge before evening cooling sets in.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Trader sentiment on the Munich August 23 high-temperature market is tightly split between 22°C (41%) and 23°C (45%), with 24°C a distant third at 9.5%.** Multiple forecasts from GFS-based and regional models converge on a maximum near these two values under clear-to-partly-cloudy skies, light northeast winds, and stable high pressure near 1023 hPa. Morning temperatures started around 8–12°C and climbed steadily through the afternoon, with hourly guidance peaking near 20–22°C at most stations. Slight differences in model timing of peak insolation and boundary-layer mixing explain the near-even odds between 22°C and 23°C, both consistent with the long-term August average high. No precipitation or significant advection is expected to alter the outcome before official DWD reporting.

Historical late-August climatology for London (~20–22 °C average maximum) provides context, but current guidance supports the observed trader weighting toward the 22–23 °C bracket ahead of any final model updates.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Official forecasts from the Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) currently project a high of 34°C for Tokyo on August 24 under partly cloudy skies with minimal precipitation chances, reflecting a strengthened Pacific high and above-normal summer temperatures across Japan.**  

Traders appear to be weighting model uncertainty, urban heat-island effects, and potential timing of cloud cover or sea breezes that could trim the peak by 1–2°C, producing the tight 32°C (37.5%) versus 33°C (28.5%) spread. Historical August maxima cluster near 31–33°C, and recent model runs show modest spread in daytime heating under variable insolation.  

Key resolution hinges on the exact recorded maximum at the official Tokyo station; any late-day clearing or stronger onshore flow would favor the lower outcomes traders currently price highest, while sustained clear conditions would support the JMA point forecast. Updated JMA guidance and short-range model consensus over the next 24 hours will likely drive the largest shifts in implied probabilities.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecasts from multiple sources, including GFS-based models, indicate a high of 23–25°C for Munich on August 24, 2026, with 23–24°C as the most probable range.** This aligns directly with the market-implied probabilities, where 24°C leads at 38.5%, followed by 23°C at 26.5% and 22°C at 14.5%.

Key scientific drivers include persistent high pressure supporting mostly clear to partly cloudy skies with easterly flow, typical late-August conditions near the long-term average high of 23.4°C. Limited daytime heating from cloud cover and moderate humidity (around 50–60%) caps peaks without major frontal passages or advection of warmer air. Model consensus shows minimal spread, with no significant revisions in the past 24–48 hours that would favor outliers like 25°C+ or sub-22°C readings.

Traders appear to weight the stable near-normal pattern heavily, though slight upward bias toward 24°C may reflect minor model variability or recent afternoon observations on August 23. Upcoming hourly data releases and any evening model runs could refine resolution criteria tied to official Munich station maxima.

**Official forecasts from the National Weather Service and other sources project a daytime high in the low 80s for New York City on August 23, 2026, aligning closely with the market’s leading outcomes around 82–83°F (46.5% implied probability) and 80–81°F (29.5%).** 

This consensus reflects typical late-August conditions, where the climatological average high is roughly 82°F, combined with today’s specific pattern of morning showers and thunderstorms transitioning to partly sunny skies. Cloud cover, scattered storms, and southeasterly winds shifting southwest (with gusts to 20 mph) are expected to limit peak heating, while dew points near 70°F add humidity that can further moderate surface temperatures. 

Recent model runs and early-morning observations show no strong heat advection or clear-sky conditions that would push readings into the mid-80s or higher, keeping 84–85°F (14%) a distant third. Historical analogs and the absence of a heat dome reinforce the narrow range around the low 80s as the most probable resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Japan Meteorological Agency forecasts for Tokyo on August 25 point to partly cloudy skies and a maximum near 34–35°C, driving the tight clustering of market-implied odds around 33–35°C. Ensemble model guidance shows modest uncertainty in peak heating due to variable cloud cover and potential sea-breeze effects along the Kanto Plain, which can cap afternoon temperatures by 1–2°C. High humidity typical of late-August conditions in the region sustains elevated heat indices, while the urban heat island effect in central Tokyo supports the upper end of the distribution. Historical climatology places late-August maxima near 31–32°C, so any deviation hinges on the strength of solar insolation and boundary-layer mixing in the next model runs. Updated JMA and global ensemble outputs expected within 24–48 hours will likely narrow the range.

Historical late-August maxima average near 31°C, yet recent seasons have featured more frequent exceedances above 32°C amid warmer baseline conditions. Fresh model updates tonight will sharpen the distinction ahead of official JMA verification.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast consensus from multiple models places Munich’s high on August 24 around 23–24 °C**, aligning with the market’s leading outcomes (24 °C at 50 %, 23 °C at 25.5 %). Official guidance and ensemble runs show a stable easterly flow under moderate high pressure, producing mostly cloudy to partly cloudy skies with minimal daytime heating. Low-level moisture and light winds limit mixing, keeping the maximum near the long-term August average of 23.4 °C. 

Precipitation chances remain low (5–6 %), reducing evaporative cooling or thunderstorm-related temperature suppression. Recent model updates through August 23 confirm this pattern with little spread, as upstream ridging and lack of strong advection suppress both warmer and cooler extremes. Higher probabilities for 25 °C or above reflect residual uncertainty in afternoon clearing, while sub-22 °C outcomes are discounted by the absence of significant cold-air advection or persistent low cloud. Traders are weighting the narrow, well-resolved temperature distribution from GFS, ECMWF, and ICON guidance.

Higher probabilities for 25 °C or above reflect residual uncertainty in afternoon clearing, while sub-22 °C outcomes are discounted by the absence of significant cold-air advection or persistent low cloud. Traders are weighting the narrow, well-resolved temperature distribution from GFS, ECMWF, and ICON guidance.

These conditions align with the market’s tight clustering around 20 °C (31.5 %) and 21 °C (25.5 %), as traders weigh the cooling effect of rain and reduced insolation against any model spread in exact timing or intensity; warmer outliers above 22 °C carry lower implied odds given the expected moderation.

Official observations from London Heathrow show midday readings near 22°C (around 72°F), with the afternoon peak expected to reach but not substantially exceed the forecast high. This reflects a stable high-pressure regime bringing clear skies and modest solar heating typical for late August, when seasonal norms run 21–23°C. 

Model consensus and surface observations indicate limited potential for 25°C or higher, as light northerly flow and the post-solstice cooling trend constrain further warming. The 23°C outcome remains plausible if daytime heating falls slightly short, consistent with its secondary market weighting, while lower or much higher results appear unlikely given current atmospheric conditions and the absence of significant forecast revisions.

Historical late-August climatology for the city centers near 22 °C, providing context for why traders assign meaningful weight to outcomes from 19 °C to 22 °C. Updated model runs and local observations over the next 48 hours will narrow the range before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Tokyo's peak temperature on August 24, 2026, centers on late-summer atmospheric conditions under a subtropical high-pressure ridge, with JMA guidance pointing to partly cloudy skies, minimal precipitation, and a daytime maximum near 34°C.** This setup favors strong solar heating during peak insolation hours, while Tokyo's urban heat island effect—driven by concrete, asphalt, and reduced evapotranspiration—typically adds 1–3°C above surrounding rural areas. High humidity (often >70%) has limited direct impact on the dry-bulb maximum but influences boundary-layer stability and model biases in surface energy balance.

Ensemble forecasts and recent model runs show a tight cluster around 32–34°C, explaining why market-implied probabilities favor 32°C (40.5%) and 33°C (36.5%) so closely. Subtle differences in predicted cloud cover, wind speed from the Pacific, or exact timing of any weak frontal passage can shift the daily maximum by 1°C. Historical late-August baselines for Tokyo average 31–32°C, but 2026's broader heat anomaly supports the higher end. Updated JMA and international model runs over the next 12–24 hours will likely resolve the narrow gap between the top two outcomes before the market closes.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Current forecasts from the Met Office and multiple models point to a daytime maximum of 22°C for London on August 24, 2026, with a tight cluster of outcomes around 21–23°C reflecting minor uncertainties in cloud cover and wind.** 

High pressure and easterly flow are delivering sunny intervals and light-to-moderate winds, supporting temperatures near or slightly above the late-August climatological average of roughly 20–22°C. Earlier in the month, London experienced well-above-normal heat (peaks near 35–38°C), but recent cooling has brought more typical conditions with clearer nights and moderate daytime heating. 

Model consensus shows limited diurnal range on the 24th due to increasing easterly winds and partial cloud, which caps insolation and prevents stronger warming. Traders assign the highest probability to 22°C because official guidance and ensemble outputs cluster there, while the 21°C and 23°C options capture plausible variations from small shifts in timing of cloud build-up or wind gusts. New forecast updates and observational data through the evening of the 23rd remain the key near-term catalysts that could refine these probabilities.

eventMetadata.context_description: Official Japan Meteorological Agency forecasts as of August 23 project a partly cloudy day with a high of 34°C for Tokyo on the 25th, aligning with the market’s leading 32.5% probability for that exact outcome. Typical late-August conditions under the Pacific high feature light winds, abundant moisture, and urban heat island amplification that routinely add 1–2°C to readings at the official Tokyo station; however, any increase in afternoon cloud cover or scattered showers—currently assigned 30% probability—could limit peak heating and shift the result toward 33°C. Ensemble guidance shows modest spread around 33–35°C depending on the precise timing of any diurnal convection, which explains the secondary 23.5% and 13.5% probabilities attached to those adjacent values. With resolution only two days away, the next model runs and updated JMA guidance will be the primary catalysts for further price movement.
